name: Spondylocostal Dysostosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Spondylocostal Dysostosis

criteria.description: Presence of multiple vertebral segmentation defects including hemivertebrae and fused vertebrae
Abnormal rib anomalies such as fused, absent, or bifid ribs
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive or dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes such as DLL3, MESP2, LFNG, or HES7

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of vertebral segmentation anomalies and rib malformations confirmed by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and radiological features are definitive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rib anomalies including fused or absent ribs

common.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to restrictive lung disease

imaging: X-ray showing vertebral segmentation defects and rib anomalies
CT scan for detailed thoracic cage assessment
genetic: Pathogenic variants in DLL3, MESP2, LFNG, HES7 genes
other: Clinical assessment of short trunk dwarfism and chest wall deformities

distinguishingFeatures: More severe rib fusion forming a 'fan-like' thoracic cage
Typically autosomal recessive inheritance with distinct genetic mutations
Cervical vertebral fusion without rib anomalies
Characteristic short neck and low posterior hairline

redFlags: Severe respiratory distress in neonatal period
Failure to thrive due to feeding difficulties
references: Turnpenny PD, et al. Spondylocostal dysostosis: clinical and molecular aspects. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2007.
Bulman MP, et al. Mutations in the human delta homologue, DLL3, cause axial skeletal defects in spondylocostal dysostosis. Nat Genet. 2000.
